Volition

voh-LISH-un · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Volition is the power or faculty of choosing one's own actions; free will.

No one forced her to resign -- she left the company entirely of her own volition.

Worked Example

The witness testified that she had signed the contract of her own volition, without any pressure from the company's lawyers.

Volition isn't a specific goal -- it's the general power or capacity to choose freely, often used in the phrase 'of one's own volition.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

free will: Free will is the power to make your own choices, and as an idea it is what philosophers debate. Volition is the lawyer's and doctor's word for that same power at work in a person, almost always in the phrase 'of one's own volition' -- stressing that nobody forced the act.

choice: A choice is a single act of selecting between options -- you make one and it is done. Volition is the underlying power that makes any choice possible in the first place: the standing capacity behind every act of choosing, not any one selection.

willpower: Willpower is the strength to stick to a decision once it is made -- to resist temptation and follow through. Volition is more basic: the power to make the decision at all. You need volition to choose a plan, and willpower to hold to it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

coercion: the practice of forcing someone to do something through pressure or threats

compulsion: an irresistible urge, often against one's own free will

Where it sits · how fully you steer your own life — preference → volition → self-determination

preference vs. volition: A preference is only a mild leaning toward one option over another -- far weaker than volition, the full power to choose your own actions.

self-determination vs. volition: Self-determination is the complete power to control one's own fate or actions, even broader than a single act of volition.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — voli-

root — voli-: will, wish (Latin velle, 'to will or wish')

suffix — -ition

suffix — -ition: the act, process, or result of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Volition comes from Latin velle ('to will or wish') -- the same root behind voluntary and volunteer. It names the simple, powerful fact of choosing something because you willed it, not because anyone made you.

Use the root in a new word: voluntary

Use the root in a new word: voluntary: Attendance at the after-school club is completely voluntary.
